title: PertReason: A Knowledge-Grounded Benchmark and Framework for Cell-State-Conditioned Mechanistic Reasoning of Perturbation Effects
claim: Current approaches predict outcomes without mechanistic reasoning; ours grounds predictions and evaluation in knowledge-graph pathways conditioned on context.
layout: 2 panels, left problem vs right solution, flow arrows, color-coded boxes
description: The figure has two halves. The left half, in dark red and gray, shows the current approach. A basal cell is perturbed by a gene or drug icon, giving a perturbed cell and effect genes. A gray cube labeled 'Current Virtual Cell' feeds expression prediction. Two red rounded boxes below state the flaws: 'No Mechanistic Reasoning' and 'Outcome-Centric Evaluation'. The right half, in blue and navy, shows the proposed framework. A perturbation icon feeds a gene regulatory knowledge graph. The cell's basal state conditions a highlighted path, which leads to the outcomes 'Up, Down, Unchanged'. Blue and navy boxes describe cell-state-conditioned pathways and ground-truth outcomes. These feed PertReasonQA and PertReasonLM through SFT/RL, then a reasoning-centric evaluation box. The eye starts at the red left side and moves to the blue right side.
caption: Overview of our proposed solutions in perturbation modeling. Current methods (left) predict expression changes without biological reasoning, limiting their evaluation to final outcomes. Our \PertReasonQA (right) leverages reasoning pathways from knowledge graphs, alongside \PertReasonLM, a reference baseline to validate the efficacy of the reasoning-centric benchmark.
abstract: Evaluating machine learning in scientific domains requires separating correct predictions from correct reasons under realistic distribution shifts. We introduce PertReason, a knowledge-grounded approach to evaluating and improving cell-state-conditioned reasoning about perturbation effects. Our framework comprises PertReasonQA, a benchmark that provides evaluation and supervision, and PertReasonLM, a reference large language model that demonstrates how such supervision supports reasoning-centric training. PertReasonQA tests whether models can generate mechanistically faithful explanations while remaining robust to complex shifts, such as new cells, unseen perturbations, cross-modal or combinatorial extrapolations. PertReasonQA combines single-cell genetic and chemical perturbation data across multiple cellular contexts with knowledge graphs, and dynamically conditions pathways on cell-specific basal states to avoid generic memorization. Evaluations of state-of-the-art models reveal systematic gaps between outcome prediction and mechanistic reasoning. As a reference probe of the benchmark, PertReasonLM is trained through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning using mechanistic supervision from PertReasonQA. PertReasonLM improves predictive accuracy and reduces answer-reason disagreement by grounding rationales in context-specific pathways. Together, we provide a diagnostic framework for exposing and mitigating failures in faithful reasoning in data-rich scientific systems. We release our datasets to support further research at https://dongkwan-kim.github.io/PertReason/.
